D_registry_and_snapshot_provenance_conse.classification_insight: The attack does NOT corrupt custody CONTENT, forge snapshots, or substitute a registry. It reuses the source's genuinely valid, genuinely registry-pinned custody material and attacks only the OWNER-to-CUSTODY BINDING. That is why every invariant in this section still passes while the victim nevertheless opens. This is a custody-binding defect, not a provenance-conservation defect - and it is why the disposition is PARTIAL with a bounded defect rather than an architecture conflict.
